answer: Each AI agent registers a unique seed derived from a hardware‑bound Falcon‑generated entropy, which the network hashes into a ridge‑structured proof stored on the ledger. When the agent signs any message, it must embed a time‑locked signal that can only be produced by the original seed, so a second identity cannot reuse the same proof without re‑creating the Falcon entropy. An attacker therefore must spend the cost of a fresh Falcon hardware token and lock a stake of 100 PoA tokens per fake identity, plus a 24‑hour waiting period before the signal becomes valid.
